en.L: And this [is] the commandment, the statutes and the judgments, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded to teach you, to do [them] in the land into which you are crossing over to take possession of it,

decisions.choice: the commandment: the whole charge Moses is about to give, in the singular
decisions.reason: The word is singular. It names the whole body of what God requires, and "the statutes and the judgments" spell out what it contains, as in 5:31 and 7:11. The same singular closes the chapter (verse 25).

decisions.choice: commanded to teach you: God commanded Moses to teach the people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say who is to teach, but 5:31 has God tell Moses, "I will speak to you all the commandment ... which you shall teach them." Moses is passing on what he was given at Horeb.

decisions.choice: you are crossing over: you are about to cross the Jordan
decisions.reason: The participle describes what is about to happen. Israel is still in Moab, east of the Jordan (4:46), and will cross into the land under Joshua (Joshua 3).

decisions.choice: commanded me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "me" from 5:31, so that it is clear who does the teaching. Literal leaves it out, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: commandment, statutes, judgments (Literal); commandment, statutes, rulings (Balanced); commands, laws, rules (Readable)
decisions.reason: The three words for the law keep the same English across Numbers to Ruth, at each level. Readable turns the singular "commandment" into "commands", since a single command would mislead a young reader; the meaning note explains the singular.

source.text: לְמַ֨עַן תִּירָ֜א אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ לִ֠שְׁמֹר אֶת־כָּל־חֻקֹּתָ֣יו וּמִצְוֺתָיו֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י מְצַוֶּךָ֒ אַתָּה֙ וּבִנְךָ֣ וּבֶן־בִּנְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּ֑יךָ וּלְמַ֖עַן יַאֲרִכֻ֥ן יָמֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: so that you may fear Yahweh your God, to keep all his statutes and his commandments which I [am] commanding you, you and your son and [the] son of your son, all [the] days of your life, and so that may be long your days.

en.L: so that you may fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments which I am commanding you, you and your {{gender:child|son}} and your {{gender:child's child|son's son}}, all the days of your life, and so that your days may be long.
en.B: so that you may fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and commandments that I am giving you, you and your {{gender:children|sons}} and {{gender:grandchildren|grandsons}}, as long as you live, and so that your life may be long.
en.R: Do this so that you will have deep respect for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God all your life, and your {{gender:children and grandchildren|sons and grandsons}} after you. Obey all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws and commands that I am giving you. Then you will live a long time.

es.R: Hazlo para que tengas un profundo respeto por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios toda tu vida, tú y tus hijos y nietos después de ti. Obedece todas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} leyes y mandatos que te doy. Así vivirás mucho tiempo.

fr.L: afin que tu craignes {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, en gardant toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} prescriptions et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements que je te commande, toi, et ton {{gender:enfant|fils}}, et l’{{gender:enfant de ton enfant|fils de ton fils}}, tous les jours de ta vie, et afin que tes jours soient prolongés.
fr.B: afin que tu craignes {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu et que tu gardes toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} prescriptions et tous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements que je te donne, toi, tes {{gender:enfants|fils}} et tes {{gender:petits-enfants|petits-fils}}, aussi longtemps que tu vivras, et afin que ta vie soit longue.
fr.R: Fais-le pour avoir un profond respect envers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu toute ta vie, toi et tes {{gender:enfants et petits-enfants|fils et petits-fils}} après toi. Obéis à toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} lois et à tous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements que je te donne. Alors tu vivras longtemps.

sw.B: ili umche {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako na kuzishika kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zote na amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} ninazokupa, wewe, watoto wako na wajukuu wako, siku zote za maisha yako, na ili uishi siku nyingi.

decisions.choice: fear: reverent awe that shows itself in obedience
decisions.reason: To fear God in Deuteronomy is not terror but the awe of those who know who he is, and it is shown by keeping his commands, as the next words say (4:10; 10:12; 17:19). The same pairing returns in verses 13 and 24.

decisions.choice: to keep: by keeping, the way fear is lived out
decisions.reason: The infinitive explains the fear just named: Israel fears God by keeping his statutes and commandments.

decisions.choice: your days may be long: you may live long (in the land)
decisions.reason: Long days means a long life, and in Deuteronomy a long life in the land God gives (4:40; 5:16, 33; 11:9).

decisions.choice: you (singular): Israel addressed as one person
decisions.reason: Verse 1 speaks to "you" in the plural; here the address turns to the singular, which runs through most of the chapter. Deuteronomy moves between the two often. The singular speaks to Israel as one people and to each member of it.

decisions.choice: have deep respect for
decisions.reason: Readable says "deep respect" for "fear", since to a young reader "fear" suggests only being afraid. Literal and Balanced keep "fear".

decisions.choice: children and grandchildren
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "grandchildren" for "your son's son"; Readable moves the generations to the end of its sentence. The Hebrew "your son and your son's son" means descendants of both sexes, so the reader's gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: {{gender:tus hijos, y los hijos de tus hijos|tu hijo, y el hijo de tu hijo}} (L); "tus hijos y tus nietos" (B, R), no span
decisions.reason: The singular "tu hijo" would name only a son, so Literal gives the inclusive plural by default, with the Hebrew singular as the setting. Balanced and Readable use the plural "hijos" and "nietos", which already include daughters and need no span.

decisions.choice: ton {{gender:enfant|fils}}, l’{{gender:enfant de ton enfant|fils de ton fils}} (L); {{gender:enfants|fils}}, {{gender:petits-enfants|petits-fils}} (B, R); "tu" from here on
decisions.reason: As the English, the generations include daughters, so the inclusive words are the default and the traditional "fils" the setting. The address turns to the singular here (m4), and French follows it with "tu".

records.literal_gloss: And you will hear, Israel, and you will take care to do, that it may go well for you and that you may increase greatly, just as spoke Yahweh, [the] God of your fathers, to you, [in a] land flowing [with] milk and honey.

en.L: Hear then, Israel, and take care to do [them], so that it may go well with you and that you may increase greatly, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, has spoken to you, [in] a land flowing [with] milk and honey.
en.B: Listen then, Israel, and keep them with care. Then all will be well with you, and you will become very many in a land flowing with milk and honey, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, has promised you.
en.R: Listen, people of Israel, and be careful to obey. Then things will go well for you. Your numbers will grow very large in a rich land, full of milk and honey, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, promised you.

es.L: Escucha, pues, Israel, y cuida de ponerlos por obra, para que te vaya bien y {{plural_you:se multipliquen|os multipliquéis}} mucho, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de tus padres, te ha dicho, [en] una tierra que fluye leche y miel.
es.B: Escucha bien, Israel, y guárdalos con cuidado. Así te irá bien y {{plural_you:llegarán|llegaréis}} a ser muy numerosos en una tierra que fluye leche y miel, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de tus padres, te ha prometido.
es.R: Escucha, pueblo de Israel, y obedece con cuidado. Así te irá bien. {{plural_you:Serán|Seréis}} muchísimos en una tierra rica, donde abundan la leche y la miel, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de tus antepasados, te lo prometió.

fr.L: Écoute donc, Israël, et veille à [les] pratiquer, afin que tout aille bien pour toi et que vous vous multipliiez grandement, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de tes pères, te l’a dit, [dans] un pays où coulent le lait et le miel.
fr.B: Écoute bien, Israël, et garde-les avec soin. Alors tout ira bien pour toi, et vous deviendrez très nombreux dans un pays où coulent le lait et le miel, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de tes pères, te l’a promis.
fr.R: Écoute, peuple d’Israël, et obéis avec soin. Alors tout ira bien pour toi. Vous deviendrez très nombreux dans un pays riche, où coulent le lait et le miel, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de tes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, te l’a promis.

sw.L: Basi sikia, Israeli, uwe mwangalifu kuyatenda, ili upate mema na mpate kuongezeka sana, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa baba zako, alivyokuambia, [katika] nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali.
sw.B: Basi sikiliza, Israeli, uyashike kwa uangalifu. Ndipo mambo yatakuendea vema, nanyi mtakuwa wengi sana katika nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa baba zako, alivyokuahidi.
sw.R: Sikiliza, Israeli, na uwe mwangalifu kutii. Ndipo mambo yatakuendea vizuri. Mtaongezeka kuwa wengi sana katika nchi tajiri, yenye maziwa na asali tele, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mababu zako, alivyokuahidi.

decisions.choice: hear: listen and take to heart
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as the first word of verse 4 and of 5:1. In Deuteronomy to hear is to listen with the intent to obey, as the next words, "take care to do", make plain.

decisions.choice: a land flowing with milk and honey: where the increase will happen
alternatives: the promise was of a land flowing with milk and honey
decisions.reason: The phrase stands at the end with no word for "in". It most likely says where Israel will grow, in the land God promised; it may also be read as the content of the promise itself (God spoke of a land flowing with milk and honey, as in Exodus 3:8, 17).

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: rich and fertile
decisions.reason: Milk speaks of good pasture for flocks and herds; honey may be wild bees' honey (Judges 14:8) or the syrup of dates and figs. Together they picture a land of plenty (Exodus 3:8; Numbers 13:27).

decisions.choice: spoke: promised
decisions.reason: What God "spoke" to the fathers is his promise to make them a great people (Genesis 12:2; 15:5; 22:17).

decisions.choice: listen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "listen" here and keep "Hear" for the confession in verse 4, which is known by that word. Literal has "Hear" in both places.

decisions.choice: "sikia" (L); "sikiliza" (B, R); "upate mema" (singular), "mpate kuongezeka" (plural)
decisions.reason: As the English keeps "Hear" for the confession in verse 4, Balanced and Readable say "sikiliza" (listen) here and keep "Sikia" for verse 4. The Hebrew "you" is singular except in "you may increase", which is plural, and Swahili follows it.

decisions.choice: hear: listen and obey
decisions.reason: The command is to listen in the full sense: to take in and to act on what is heard (verse 3; 5:1; 9:1). From this first word the confession of verses 4-9 came to be called the Shema, "Hear". On reciting it morning and evening see verse 7.

decisions.choice: the LORD our God, the LORD is one
alternatives: the LORD is our God, the LORD is one
the LORD our God is one LORD
the LORD is our God, the LORD alone
decisions.reason: The four Hebrew words have no verb, so they can be grouped in more than one way. Read as the text is set here, they say that Israel's God is one: one God, not many, undivided and without rival. The confession of Mark 12:29-32 takes them this way. Another reading groups them "the LORD is our God, the LORD is one", or "the LORD is our God, the LORD alone" (see the next note). Each reading says something the rest of Deuteronomy teaches (4:35, 39; 5:7).

decisions.choice: one: one and unique
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for "one". It can also mean "alone, the only one" (1 Chronicles 29:1). Read that way the verse says that the LORD alone is Israel's God, so that Israel must worship no other god (5:7; 6:14). Read as "one", it says that he is the one God. Zechariah 14:9 uses the same words for the day when "the LORD will be one, and his name one".

decisions.choice: quoted by Jesus as the first commandment (Mark 12:29-30)
decisions.reason: Asked which commandment is first of all, Jesus quotes verses 4-5 (Mark 12:29-30), and the scribe answers that God is one and there is no other besides him (Mark 12:32, echoing 4:35). Matthew 22:37 and Luke 10:27 quote verse 5.

decisions.choice: Hear, Israel:
decisions.reason: "Hear" rather than "Listen", because the confession is known by its first word, and no "O" before "Israel", which modern English does not use when calling someone by name.

decisions.choice: the same words as Balanced
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the Balanced wording. Any plainer rewording would have to choose one of the readings set out in the notes, and the levels may not differ in meaning.

decisions.choice: Escucha, Israel: ... es uno (the same words at every level)
decisions.reason: "Escucha" is the ordinary verb for hearing that takes in and heeds (m1); no "oh" before Israel. "Es uno" keeps the Hebrew open to the readings in m2 and m3, where "el único" would choose one, so Readable keeps the Balanced wording, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Écoute, Israël : ... est un (the same words at every level)
decisions.reason: French has one verb for hear and listen, so "Écoute" stands at every level, without "ô". "Est un" keeps the Hebrew open to the readings in m2 and m3; "le seul" or "unique" would choose one of them, and the levels may not differ in meaning, so Readable keeps the Balanced wording, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Sikia, Israeli: ... ni mmoja (the same words at every level)
decisions.reason: "Sikia" (hear) is kept for the confession, as the English keeps "Hear", with no "Ee" before Israel. "Ni mmoja" keeps the Hebrew open to the readings in m2 and m3; "peke yake" would choose one, so Readable keeps the Balanced wording, as the English does.

en.R: Love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all that you are: with all your heart, with all your life, and with all your strength.

fr.B: Tu dois aimer {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu de tout ton cœur, de tout ton être et de toutes tes forces.
fr.R: Aime {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu avec tout ce que tu es : de tout ton cœur, de toute ta vie et de toutes tes forces.

sw.L: Nawe utampenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako kwa moyo wako wote, na kwa nafsi yako yote, na kwa uwezo wako wote.
sw.B: Mpende {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako kwa moyo wako wote, kwa nafsi yako yote, na kwa nguvu zako zote.
sw.R: Mpende {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako kwa utu wako wote: kwa moyo wako wote, kwa maisha yako yote, na kwa nguvu zako zote.

decisions.choice: love: wholehearted loyalty shown in obedience
decisions.reason: The love commanded here is devotion that can be asked for: loyalty to God that is lived out in keeping his commands (5:10; 7:9; 10:12; 11:1, 13). It answers his love for Israel (7:8; 10:15) and includes the heart's affection, not only outward duty.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, mind and will
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where a person thinks, decides and wants, not only where one feels (8:2; 29:3).

decisions.choice: soul: life, the whole living self
decisions.reason: The word means the living person, a person's life and desires (12:20; 24:6). It is not a part of a person set against the body.

decisions.choice: strength, power: everything one has and can do
decisions.reason: The word normally means "very" or "much". Used as a noun, here and in 2 Kings 23:25 (of King Josiah, who turned to the LORD with all his heart, soul and strength), it means one's "muchness": all one's power and means. The three phrases together ask for love with the whole person.

decisions.choice: the greatest commandment (Mark 12:30; Matthew 22:37; Luke 10:27)
decisions.reason: Jesus names this verse as the first and greatest commandment and joins to it Leviticus 19:18, "love your neighbor as yourself".

decisions.choice: whole being (Balanced); all your life (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "soul". Balanced and Readable avoid it, because "soul" suggests to many readers only the spiritual part of a person, while the Hebrew means the whole living self.

decisions.choice: with all that you are
decisions.reason: Readable says first what the list of three adds up to, then names the three.

decisions.choice: alma (L), ser (B), vida (R); poder (L), fuerzas (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English, Literal keeps "alma" and Balanced and Readable say the whole living self (m3); Literal "poder" follows the English "power" (m4).

decisions.choice: âme (L), être (B), vie (R); puissance (L), forces (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English, Literal keeps "âme" and Balanced and Readable say the whole living self (m3). Literal "puissance" follows the English "power" for the rare noun "muchness" (m4); Balanced and Readable say "de toutes tes forces".

decisions.choice: nafsi (L, B), maisha (R); uwezo (L), nguvu (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Nafsi" already means the living self, not a spiritual part (m3), so Balanced keeps it where the English moves from "soul" to "whole being"; "roho" would suggest the spirit. Readable says "maisha", as the English says "life".

source.text: וְהָי֞וּ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֧י מְצַוְּךָ֛ הַיּ֖וֹם עַל־לְבָבֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be these words which I [am] commanding you today on your heart.

en.L: And they shall be, these words which I am commanding you today, on your heart.
en.B: Keep these words that I am commanding you today close to your heart.
en.R: Always remember these words I am giving you today. Keep them in your heart.

es.L: Y estarán estas palabras que hoy te ordeno sobre tu corazón.
es.B: Guarda muy cerca de tu corazón estas palabras que hoy te ordeno.
es.R: Recuerda siempre estas palabras que hoy te doy. Guárdalas en tu corazón.

fr.L: Et elles seront, ces paroles que je te commande aujourd’hui, sur ton cœur.
fr.B: Garde tout près de ton cœur ces paroles que je te prescris aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Souviens-toi toujours de ces paroles que je te donne aujourd’hui. Garde-les dans ton cœur.

sw.L: Na maneno haya ninayokuamuru leo yatakuwa juu ya moyo wako.
sw.B: Yaweke karibu na moyo wako maneno haya ninayokuamuru leo.
sw.R: Kumbuka daima maneno haya ninayokupa leo. Yatunze moyoni mwako.

decisions.choice: these words: the words just spoken, and with them all Moses teaches
decisions.reason: The words are first of all the confession and command of verses 4-5. Through the rest of the book "these words" also stand for the whole law Moses is setting out (5:22; 11:18).

decisions.choice: on your heart: remembered, taken in, thought about
decisions.reason: What is on the heart is held in the mind and shapes what one does (11:18; 30:14; Proverbs 3:3).

decisions.choice: close to your heart (Balanced); always remember ... keep them in your heart (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the picture into an English one with the same sense; Readable says plainly that the words are to be remembered.

source.text: וְשִׁנַּנְתָּ֣ם לְבָנֶ֔יךָ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֖ בָּ֑ם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ֤ בְּבֵיתֶ֨ךָ֙ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ֣ בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וּֽבְשָׁכְבְּךָ֖ וּבְקוּמֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will repeat them to your sons and you will speak of them in your sitting in your house and in your walking on the road and in your lying down and in your rising.

en.L: And you shall repeat them to your {{gender:children|sons}} and speak of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road and when you lie down and when you rise up.
en.B: Teach them carefully to your {{gender:children|sons}}, and speak of them as you sit in your house and as you go on your way, as you lie down and as you rise.
en.R: Teach them to your {{gender:children|sons}} over and over. Talk about them at home and when you are out traveling, at night when you go to bed and in the morning when you get up.

es.L: Y se las repetirás a tus hijos, y hablarás de ellas al sentarte en tu casa y al andar por el camino, al acostarte y al levantarte.
es.B: Enséñaselas con insistencia a tus hijos, y habla de ellas tanto sentado en casa como de camino, tanto al acostarte como al levantarte.
es.R: Enséñaselas a tus hijos una y otra vez. Habla de ellas en casa y cuando sales de viaje, por la noche al irte a dormir y por la mañana al levantarte.

fr.L: Et tu les répéteras à tes {{gender:enfants|fils}}, et tu en parleras quand tu seras assis dans ta maison, et quand tu marcheras sur la route, et quand tu te coucheras, et quand tu te lèveras.
fr.B: Enseigne-les avec soin à tes {{gender:enfants|fils}} et parles-en, assis dans ta maison comme en chemin, au coucher comme au lever.
fr.R: Enseigne-les sans cesse à tes {{gender:enfants|fils}}. Parles-en à la maison et en voyage, le soir quand tu vas te coucher et le matin quand tu te lèves.

sw.L: Nawe utayarudia kwa watoto wako, na kuyazungumza unapoketi nyumbani mwako na unapotembea barabarani, unapolala na unapoamka.
sw.B: Wafundishe watoto wako kwa bidii, na uyazungumze ukiwa umeketi nyumbani au ukiwa safarini, wakati wa kulala na wakati wa kuamka.
sw.R: Wafundishe watoto wako tena na tena. Yazungumze ukiwa nyumbani na ukiwa safarini, usiku unapokwenda kulala na asubuhi unapoamka.

decisions.choice: repeat: teach by repeating, drill in
decisions.reason: The verb elsewhere means to sharpen (Psalm 64:4). In this form it is found only here, and means to go over the words again and again until they are learned.

decisions.choice: sitting and walking, lying down and rising: always and everywhere
decisions.reason: The pairs name opposites to cover the whole of life: at home and away, at night and in the morning. The words are to be spoken of at all times, not only on set occasions.

decisions.choice: when you lie down and when you rise: the later practice of reciting the Shema
decisions.reason: From these words Jewish practice came to recite verses 4-9, with 11:13-21 and Numbers 15:37-41, each evening and each morning.

decisions.choice: your sons: your children
decisions.reason: The plural "sons" here means children in general, daughters as well as sons, and the reader's gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: over and over; out traveling; at night ... in the morning
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the verb and the paired phrases mean.

decisions.choice: "tus hijos", no gender span
decisions.reason: The plural "hijos" already includes daughters (m4), so Spanish has no second wording for the gender setting; Swahili "watoto" likewise. French has the span, "{{gender:enfants|fils}}".

source.text: וּקְשַׁרְתָּ֥ם לְא֖וֹת עַל־יָדֶ֑ךָ וְהָי֥וּ לְטֹטָפֹ֖ת בֵּ֥ין עֵינֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will bind them for a sign on your hand, and they will be for frontlets between your eyes.

en.L: And you shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes.
en.B: Tie them as a sign on your hand, and let them be a band between your eyes.
en.R: Tie them on your hand as a reminder, and wear them as a band on your forehead.

es.L: Y las atarás por señal sobre tu mano, y serán por frontales entre tus ojos.
es.B: Átalas a tu mano como señal, y que sean una banda entre tus ojos.
es.R: Átatelas en la mano como recordatorio, y llévalas como una banda en la frente.

fr.L: Et tu les attacheras pour signe sur ta main, et elles seront pour fronteaux entre tes yeux.
fr.B: Attache-les à ta main comme un signe, et qu’elles soient un bandeau entre tes yeux.
fr.R: Attache-les à ta main pour t’en souvenir, et porte-les comme un bandeau sur ton front.

sw.L: Nawe utayafunga yawe ishara juu ya mkono wako, nayo yatakuwa utepe kati ya macho yako.
sw.B: Yafunge mkononi mwako kama ishara, na yawe utepe kati ya macho yako.
sw.R: Yafunge mkononi mwako ili yakukumbushe, na uyavae kama utepe kwenye paji la uso wako.

decisions.choice: a sign on your hand: the words kept always before you
alternatives: a command to wear the words written out
decisions.reason: The words may be meant as a picture, as in Proverbs 3:3, 6:21 and 7:3, where teaching is bound on the neck or the fingers, or as a command to wear them. In Exodus 13:9 and 16 the sign is the feast itself. Later Jewish practice took this verse literally: phylacteries, small boxes holding written passages (among them 6:4-9 and 11:13-21), are worn on the arm and the forehead (compare Matthew 23:5).

decisions.choice: frontlets: a band or mark worn on the forehead
decisions.reason: As at Exodus 13:16, the word is rare and its meaning not certain: a headband, an ornament or a mark. "Between your eyes" means on the forehead.

decisions.choice: as a reminder; on your forehead
decisions.reason: Readable says what a sign is for and where "between your eyes" is.

source.text: וּכְתַבְתָּ֛ם עַל־מְזוּזֹ֥ת בֵּיתֶ֖ךָ וּבִשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you will write them on [the] doorposts of your house and on your gates.

en.L: And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house and upon your gates.
en.B: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on the gates of your town.
en.R: Write them where you will see them: on the doorposts of your houses and on the gates of your towns.

es.L: Y las escribirás sobre los postes de la puerta de tu casa y sobre tus puertas.
es.B: Escríbelas en los postes de la puerta de tu casa y en las puertas de tu ciudad.
es.R: Escríbelas donde las veas: en los marcos de las puertas de tus casas y en las entradas de tus ciudades.

fr.L: Et tu les écriras sur les montants de ta maison et sur tes portes.
fr.B: Écris-les sur les montants de porte de ta maison et sur les portes de ta ville.
fr.R: Écris-les là où tu les verras : sur les montants de porte de tes maisons et aux portes de tes villes.

sw.L: Nawe utayaandika kwenye miimo ya nyumba yako na kwenye malango yako.
sw.B: Yaandike kwenye miimo ya milango ya nyumba yako na kwenye malango ya mji wako.
sw.R: Yaandike mahali utakapoyaona: kwenye miimo ya milango ya nyumba zako na kwenye malango ya miji yako.

decisions.choice: doorposts: the side posts of a house door
decisions.reason: The words are to mark every home. The Hebrew word for doorpost, mezuzah, became the name of the small case holding verses 4-9 and 11:13-21 that Jewish homes fix to the doorpost, following this verse and 11:20.

decisions.choice: your gates: the gates of your towns
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy "your gates" are the gates of the towns Israel will live in, where people came and went and the elders judged (5:14; 16:18; 21:19). Within the gates is within the town.

decisions.choice: the gates of your town
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose gates are meant; Readable adds why the words are written there.

source.text: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּ֥י יְבִיאֲךָ֣׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אֶל־הָאָ֜רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֧ע לַאֲבֹתֶ֛יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם לְיִצְחָ֥ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לָ֣תֶת לָ֑ךְ עָרִ֛ים גְּדֹלֹ֥ת וְטֹבֹ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־בָנִֽיתָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be when brings you Yahweh your God to the land which he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to you, cities great and good which you did not build,

en.L: And it shall be, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brings you into the land that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to you, great and good cities which you did not build,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is bringing you into the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would give you. It has great and fine cities that you did not build,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you into the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would give you. There you will find large, fine cities that you did not build.

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te haga entrar en la tierra que juró a tus padres, a Abraham, a Isaac y a Jacob, que te daría, ciudades grandes y buenas que tú no edificaste,
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te va a hacer entrar en la tierra que juró a tus padres, a Abraham, Isaac y Jacob, que te daría. Hay allí ciudades grandes y hermosas que tú no construiste,
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te llevará a la tierra que prometió a tus antepasados Abraham, Isaac y Jacob que te daría. Allí encontrarás ciudades grandes y hermosas que tú no construiste.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’aura fait entrer dans le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a juré à tes pères, à Abraham, à Isaac et à Jacob, de te donner, des villes grandes et bonnes que tu n’as pas bâties,
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu va te faire entrer dans le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a juré à tes pères, à Abraham, Isaac et Jacob, de te donner. Il y a là des villes grandes et belles que tu n’as pas bâties,
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu va te faire entrer dans le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis à tes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} Abraham, Isaac et Jacob de te donner. Tu y trouveras de grandes et belles villes que tu n’as pas construites.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapokuingiza katika nchi aliyowaapia baba zako, Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo, kwamba atakupa, miji mikubwa na mizuri ambayo hukuijenga,
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakuingiza katika nchi aliyowaapia baba zako, Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo, kwamba atakupa. Ina miji mikubwa na mizuri ambayo hukuijenga,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakuingiza katika nchi aliyowaahidi mababu zako Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo kwamba atakupa. Huko utakuta miji mikubwa na mizuri ambayo hukuijenga.

decisions.choice: the land he swore to your fathers: the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: God promised the land on oath to Abraham (Genesis 12:7; 15:18; 22:16-17), to Isaac (26:3) and to Jacob (28:13), and Joseph recalled the oath as he died (50:24). Deuteronomy often grounds the gift of the land in this oath (1:8; 6:18, 23).

decisions.choice: one sentence from verse 10 to verse 12
decisions.reason: "When the LORD your God brings you ..." opens a long sentence. Verses 10-11 list what Israel will receive without working for it; the main clause, the warning not to forget the LORD, comes in verse 12.

decisions.choice: good cities: fine, prosperous cities
decisions.reason: "Good" here describes cities well built and well off, as "every good thing" in verse 11 means riches and goods.

decisions.choice: separate sentences; promised
decisions.reason: Balanced divides the long sentence into two, with the warning starting at the end of verse 11; Readable breaks it into short sentences and says "promised" for "swore". Literal keeps one sentence running into verse 12.

source.text: וּבָ֨תִּ֜ים מְלֵאִ֣ים כָּל־טוּב֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־מִלֵּאתָ֒ וּבֹרֹ֤ת חֲצוּבִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־חָצַ֔בְתָּ כְּרָמִ֥ים וְזֵיתִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־נָטָ֑עְתָּ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ וְשָׂבָֽעְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and houses full of every good thing which you did not fill, and cisterns hewn which you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, and you will eat and you will be satisfied,

en.L: and houses full of every good thing which you did not fill, and cisterns hewn out which you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, and you eat and are satisfied,
en.B: houses full of every kind of good thing that you did not put in them, cisterns cut in the rock that you did not cut, vineyards and olive groves you did not plant. When you have eaten your fill,
en.R: You will find houses full of good things that you did not put there. You will find pits cut into the rock to hold rainwater, which you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant. You will eat all you want.

es.L: y casas llenas de todo bien que tú no llenaste, y cisternas excavadas que tú no excavaste, viñas y olivos que tú no plantaste, y comerás y te saciarás,
es.B: casas llenas de toda clase de bienes que tú no pusiste en ellas, cisternas cavadas en la roca que tú no cavaste, viñas y olivares que tú no plantaste. Cuando hayas comido hasta saciarte,
es.R: Encontrarás casas llenas de cosas buenas que tú no pusiste allí. Encontrarás pozos excavados en la roca para guardar el agua de lluvia, que tú no cavaste, y viñas y olivos que tú no plantaste. Comerás todo lo que quieras.

fr.L: et des maisons pleines de toutes bonnes choses que tu n’as pas remplies, et des citernes creusées que tu n’as pas creusées, des vignes et des oliviers que tu n’as pas plantés, et tu mangeras et tu seras rassasié,
fr.B: des maisons pleines de toutes sortes de biens que tu n’y as pas mis, des citernes taillées dans le roc que tu n’as pas taillées, des vignes et des oliveraies que tu n’as pas plantées. Quand tu auras mangé à satiété,
fr.R: Tu trouveras des maisons pleines de bonnes choses que tu n’y as pas mises. Tu trouveras des trous creusés dans le rocher pour garder l’eau de pluie, que tu n’as pas creusés, et des vignes et des oliviers que tu n’as pas plantés. Tu mangeras autant que tu voudras.

sw.L: na nyumba zilizojaa kila kitu kizuri ambazo hukuzijaza, na visima vilivyochongwa ambavyo hukuvichonga, mashamba ya mizabibu na mizeituni ambayo hukuipanda, nawe utakula na kushiba,
sw.B: nyumba zilizojaa kila aina ya vitu vizuri ambavyo hukuviweka, visima vilivyochongwa mwambani ambavyo hukuvichonga, mashamba ya mizabibu na ya mizeituni ambayo hukuyapanda. Utakapokuwa umekula na kushiba,
sw.R: Utakuta nyumba zilizojaa vitu vizuri ambavyo hukuviweka humo. Utakuta mashimo yaliyochongwa mwambani kuhifadhi maji ya mvua, ambayo hukuyachimba, na mashamba ya mizabibu na mizeituni ambayo hukuyapanda. Utakula kadiri unavyotaka.

decisions.choice: cisterns hewn out: pits cut into rock to store rainwater
decisions.reason: In the hill country, where springs were few, households and towns cut pits in the rock and plastered them to collect the winter rains. A cistern took long, hard labor to make; Israel would find them ready.

decisions.choice: you eat and are satisfied: still part of the "when" clause
decisions.reason: Eating one's fill is the last of the things that will happen when Israel enters the land; the warning follows in verse 12. Chapter 8 makes the same point: full and comfortable, Israel may forget who gave the plenty (8:10-14).

decisions.choice: pits cut into the rock to hold rainwater
decisions.reason: Readable explains "cisterns", a word many young readers will not know.

source.text: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֔ פֶּן־תִּשְׁכַּ֖ח אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצִֽיאֲךָ֛ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Take heed to yourself lest you forget Yahweh who brought you out from [the] land of Egypt, from [a] house of slaves.

en.L: take heed to yourself lest you forget {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.
en.B: then watch yourself, so that you do not forget {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
en.R: When that happens, be careful! Do not forget {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who brought you out of Egypt, where you were slaves.

es.L: guárdate, no sea que olvides {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, que te hizo salir de la tierra de Egipto, de la casa de esclavos.
es.B: entonces cuídate de no olvidar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, que te sacó del país de Egipto, de la casa de esclavitud.
es.R: Cuando eso ocurra, ¡ten cuidado! No te olvides {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que te sacó de Egipto, donde eras esclavo.

fr.L: garde-toi, de peur que tu n’oublies {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui t’a fait sortir du pays d’Égypte, de la maison des esclaves.
fr.B: alors prends garde à toi, pour ne pas oublier {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui t’a fait sortir du pays d’Égypte, de la maison d’esclavage.
fr.R: Quand cela arrivera, fais attention ! N’oublie pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui t’a fait sortir d’Égypte, où tu étais esclave.

sw.L: jihadhari nafsi yako usije ukamsahau {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliyekutoa katika nchi ya Misri, katika nyumba ya watumwa.
sw.B: basi jilinde, usije ukamsahau {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliyekutoa katika nchi ya Misri, katika nyumba ya utumwa.
sw.R: Hayo yatakapotokea, uwe mwangalifu! Usimsahau {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliyekutoa Misri, ulikokuwa mtumwa.

decisions.choice: take heed to yourself: be on your guard
decisions.reason: The phrase means to watch oneself closely, as in 4:9, 23 and 8:11.

decisions.choice: forget the LORD: stop depending on him and stop obeying him
decisions.reason: To forget God is not a lapse of memory but turning away from him, as 8:11-18 explains: Israel might think its wealth came by its own strength.

decisions.choice: house of slaves / slavery; slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" stays at every level for Israel's slavery in Egypt, as the style guide sets out (Exodus 20:2; Deuteronomy 5:6).

source.text: אֶת־יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ תִּירָ֖א וְאֹת֣וֹ תַעֲבֹ֑ד וּבִשְׁמ֖וֹ תִּשָּׁבֵֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh your God you will fear, and him you will serve, and by his name you will swear.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God you shall fear, and {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you shall serve, and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name you shall swear.
en.B: Fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and no other; serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and swear your oaths by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is the one you must fear and serve. When you make a promise with an oath, use only {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

es.L: {{divine_name:Al SEÑOR|A Yahvé}} tu Dios temerás, y a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} servirás, y por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre jurarás.
es.B: Teme {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios y a ningún otro; a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sirve, y jura por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.R: Es {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios a quien debes temer y servir. Cuando hagas una promesa con juramento, usa solo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.

fr.L: C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu que tu craindras, et c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que tu serviras, et c’est par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom que tu jureras.
fr.B: Crains {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu et nul autre ; sers-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}, et prête serment par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.R: C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu que tu dois craindre et servir. Quand tu fais une promesse avec serment, utilise seulement {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako utamcha, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} utamtumikia, na kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} utaapa.
sw.B: Umche {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, wala si mwingine; umtumikie {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, na uape kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako ndiye unayepaswa kumcha na kumtumikia. Unapoahidi kwa kiapo, tumia jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} tu.

decisions.choice: the LORD ... him ... his name: placed first for emphasis
decisions.reason: Each clause puts God before its verb: the LORD and no other is to be feared, served and sworn by. Verse 14 makes the contrast explicit.

decisions.choice: serve: worship and obey
decisions.reason: To serve a god is to worship him and live under his rule (5:9; 10:12, 20).

decisions.choice: swear by his name: make oaths calling on the LORD as witness
decisions.reason: An oath called on a god to witness and enforce a promise. To swear by the LORD's name acknowledged him as Israel's God; to swear by other gods was to honor them (10:20; Joshua 23:7; Jeremiah 12:16).

decisions.choice: quoted by Jesus in the wilderness (Matthew 4:10; Luke 4:8)
decisions.reason: When he is tempted to worship the devil, Jesus answers with this verse in its Greek form, which reads "worship" and adds "only". He also answers from verse 16 (Matthew 4:7) and from 8:3.

decisions.choice: and no other (Balanced); use only his name (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say with "no other" and "only" what the Hebrew says by putting the LORD first in each clause.

source.text: לֹ֣א תֵֽלְכ֔וּן אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים מֵאֱלֹהֵי֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר סְבִיבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you will go after other gods, from [the] gods of the peoples which [are] around you.

en.L: You shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples who [are] around you.
en.B: You must not go after other gods, any of the gods of the peoples that surround you.
en.R: Do not worship other gods, the gods of the nations that live around you.

es.L: No {{plural_you:irán|iréis}} tras otros dioses, de los dioses de los pueblos que [están] alrededor de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} seguir a otros dioses, a ninguno de los dioses de los pueblos que {{plural_you:los|os}} rodean.
es.R: No {{plural_you:adoren|adoréis}} a otros dioses, los dioses de las naciones que viven alrededor de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Vous n’irez pas après d’autres dieux, d’entre les dieux des peuples qui [sont] autour de vous.
fr.B: Vous ne suivrez pas d’autres dieux, aucun des dieux des peuples qui vous entourent.
fr.R: N’adorez pas d’autres dieux, les dieux des nations qui vivent autour de vous.

sw.L: Hamtaifuata miungu mingine, katika miungu ya watu [walio] kuwazunguka.
sw.B: Msiifuate miungu mingine, yoyote kati ya miungu ya watu wanaowazunguka.
sw.R: Msiiabudu miungu mingine, miungu ya mataifa yanayoishi kandokando yenu.

decisions.choice: go after: follow as a worshiper
decisions.reason: To walk after a god is to give it one's loyalty and worship (8:19; 11:28; 13:3).

decisions.choice: you (plural)
decisions.reason: Here the address turns to the plural again, as in verse 1; the command applies to every member of the people.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says what "go after" means.

source.text: כִּ֣י אֵ֥ל קַנָּ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בְּקִרְבֶּ֑ךָ פֶּן־יֶ֠חֱרֶה אַף־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּ֔ךְ וְהִשְׁמִ֣ידְךָ֔ מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For a God jealous [is] Yahweh your God in your midst, lest burn [the] anger of Yahweh your God against you and he destroy you from on [the] face of the ground.

en.L: For a jealous God [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in your midst, lest the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God burn against you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroy you from on the face of the ground.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who is in your midst, is a jealous God; beware, or the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will blaze against you and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will wipe you off the face of the earth.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who lives among you, is a jealous God. If you worship other gods, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will become very angry with you and wipe you off the face of the earth.

es.L: Porque un Dios celoso [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios en medio de ti, no sea que se encienda la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios contra ti y te destruya de sobre la faz de la tierra.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, que está en medio de ti, es un Dios celoso; ten cuidado, o la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios arderá contra ti y te borrará de la faz de la tierra.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, que vive en medio de ti, es un Dios celoso. Si adoras a otros dioses, se enojará mucho contigo y te borrará de la faz de la tierra.

fr.L: Car un Dieu jaloux, [c’est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu au milieu de toi, de peur que la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu ne s’enflamme contre toi et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne te détruise de dessus la face du sol.
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, qui est au milieu de toi, est un Dieu jaloux ; prends garde, sinon la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu s’enflammera contre toi et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’effacera de la face de la terre.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, qui vit au milieu de toi, est un Dieu jaloux. Si tu adores d’autres dieux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mettra très en colère contre toi et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te fera disparaître de la surface de la terre.

sw.L: Kwa maana Mungu mwenye wivu [ndiye] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako aliye katikati yako, isije hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako ikawaka juu yako, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akakuangamiza kutoka juu ya uso wa ardhi.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, aliye katikati yako, ni Mungu mwenye wivu; jihadhari, la sivyo hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako itawaka dhidi yako, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atakufutilia mbali kutoka uso wa dunia.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, anayeishi katikati yako, ni Mungu mwenye wivu. Ukiabudu miungu mingine, atakukasirikia sana na kukufutilia mbali kutoka uso wa dunia.

decisions.choice: a jealous God: one who will not share his people's loyalty with other gods
decisions.reason: The word describes God's rightful claim on Israel, like a husband's claim on a faithful wife. It is not envy but zeal for what is his (4:24; 5:9; Exodus 20:5; 34:14).

decisions.choice: the anger burns: anger flares up
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of anger burning, a common picture of sudden, strong anger (7:4; 11:17).

decisions.choice: the face of the ground: the earth
decisions.reason: The word can mean the soil, the land of Israel or the whole earth. Here it may be the land Israel is entering, from which it would be removed (28:63), or the earth as in 7:6.

decisions.choice: in your midst: present among his people
decisions.reason: God is close at hand among Israel (7:21; 23:15), so their loyalty and their sin are both before him.

decisions.choice: If you worship other gods
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition that "lest" leaves implied from verse 14.

source.text: לֹ֣א תְנַסּ֔וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִסִּיתֶ֖ם בַּמַּסָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you will test Yahweh your God just as you tested [him] at Massah.

en.L: You shall not put {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to the test, just as you tested [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] at Massah.
en.B: You must not put {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to the test, as you tested {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at Massah.
en.R: Do not test {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God the way you did at Massah, when you doubted that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with you.

es.L: No {{plural_you:pondrán|pondréis}} a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, tal como [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] {{plural_you:pusieron|pusisteis}} a prueba en Masá.
es.B: No {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} poner a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, como {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:probaron|probasteis}} en Masá.
es.R: No {{plural_you:pongan|pongáis}} a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} como lo {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} en Masá, cuando {{plural_you:dudaron|dudasteis}} de que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estuviera con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Vous ne mettrez pas à l’épreuve {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu, comme vous [{{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}]avez éprouvé à Massa.
fr.B: Vous ne devez pas mettre à l’épreuve {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu, comme vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez éprouvé à Massa.
fr.R: Ne mettez pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu à l’épreuve comme vous l’avez fait à Massa, quand vous doutiez qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit avec vous.

sw.L: Hamtamjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, kama mlivyomjaribu huko Masa.
sw.B: Msimjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, kama mlivyomjaribu huko Masa.
sw.R: Msimjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu kama mlivyofanya huko Masa, mlipotilia shaka kwamba yuko pamoja nanyi.

decisions.choice: test: demand that God prove himself
decisions.reason: To test God is to doubt his care and demand proof of it, as Israel did when it had no water (Exodus 17:2, 7; Numbers 14:22; Psalm 95:8-9).

decisions.choice: Massah: the place called "Testing"
decisions.reason: At Rephidim the people quarreled with Moses over water and asked, "Is the LORD among us or not?" Moses named the place Massah, "testing" (Exodus 17:1-7; compare 9:22; 33:8).

decisions.choice: quoted by Jesus in the wilderness (Matthew 4:7; Luke 4:12)
decisions.reason: When he is tempted to throw himself from the temple, Jesus answers with this command.

decisions.choice: when you doubted that he was with you
decisions.reason: Readable says what happened at Massah, from Exodus 17:7.

source.text: שָׁמ֣וֹר תִּשְׁמְר֔וּן אֶת־מִצְוֺ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְעֵדֹתָ֥יו וְחֻקָּ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Carefully you will keep [the] commandments of Yahweh your God and his testimonies and his statutes which he commanded you.

en.L: You shall diligently keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has commanded you.
en.B: Take care to keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has commanded you.
en.R: Be careful to obey the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and the instructions and laws {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Guardarán|Guardaréis}} cuidadosamente los mandamientos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} testimonios y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} estatutos que te ha mandado.
es.B: {{plural_you:Cuiden|Cuidad}} de guardar los mandamientos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} decretos y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} estatutos, que te ha ordenado.
es.R: {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de obedecer los mandamientos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, y las instrucciones y leyes que {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado.

fr.L: Vous garderez soigneusement les commandements {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} témoignages et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} prescriptions qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’a commandés.
fr.B: Veillez à garder les commandements {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} décrets et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} prescriptions, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’a donnés.
fr.R: Faites bien attention à obéir aux commandements {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu, et aux instructions et aux lois qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a données.

sw.L: Mtazishika kwa bidii amri za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, na shuhuda {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} alizokuamuru.
sw.B: Kuweni waangalifu kuzishika amri za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, masharti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, alizokuamuru.
sw.R: Hakikisheni mnatii amri za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, na maelekezo na sheria alizowapa.

decisions.choice: diligently keep: keep with care
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: "keeping, you shall keep".

decisions.choice: testimonies: solemn charges given before witnesses
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root for witness. It names the terms of the covenant, solemnly declared (4:45; 6:20).

decisions.choice: testimonies (Literal); decrees (Balanced); instructions (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word's link to witness; Balanced and Readable use words that a reader takes as commands.

decisions.choice: Be careful to obey
decisions.reason: Readable says "obey" for "keep".

decisions.choice: testimonios (L); decretos (B); instrucciones (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the link with witness, Balanced and Readable use words read as commands. "Te ha mandado" is singular at Literal and Balanced, as the Hebrew; Readable keeps the plural.

decisions.choice: témoignages (L); décrets (B); instructions (R); "vous", then "t'a commandés" (L, B)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the link with witness, Balanced and Readable use words read as commands. The Hebrew "you" is plural except in "he has commanded you", which is singular, and Literal and Balanced follow it; Readable keeps the plural through the sentence.

decisions.choice: shuhuda (L); masharti (B); maelekezo (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the link with "shahidi" (witness); Balanced says "masharti", the terms of the covenant, since "maagizo" already stands for the rulings (mishpatim) in Deuteronomy; Readable says "maelekezo" (instructions), as the English.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֛יתָ הַיָּשָׁ֥ר וְהַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ וּבָ֗אתָ וְיָֽרַשְׁתָּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטֹּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לַאֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will do the right and the good in [the] eyes of Yahweh, so that it may go well for you and you will go in and you will take possession of the land the good which swore Yahweh to your fathers,

en.L: And you shall do what [is] right and good in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that it may go well with you, and you may go in and take possession of the good land which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers,
en.B: Do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sees as right and good, so that all will be well with you and you can enter and take possession of the good land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers,
en.R: Do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says is right and good. Then things will go well for you. You will go in and take for your own the good land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised your ancestors with an oath.

es.L: Y harás lo [que es] recto y bueno a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, para que te vaya bien, y entres y tomes posesión de la buena tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juró a tus padres,
es.B: Haz lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} considera recto y bueno, para que te vaya bien y puedas entrar y tomar posesión de la buena tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juró a tus padres,
es.R: Haz lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice que es recto y bueno. Así te irá bien. Entrarás y tomarás como tuya la buena tierra que prometió con juramento a tus antepasados.

fr.L: Et tu feras ce qui [est] droit et bon aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, afin que tout aille bien pour toi, et que tu entres et prennes possession du bon pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a juré à tes pères,
fr.B: Fais ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} considère comme droit et bon, afin que tout aille bien pour toi et que tu puisses entrer et prendre possession du bon pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a juré à tes pères,
fr.R: Fais ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} déclare juste et bon. Alors tout ira bien pour toi. Tu entreras dans le bon pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis par serment à tes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, et tu le prendras pour toi.

sw.L: Nawe utafanya yaliyo sawa na mema machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ili upate mema, na uingie na kuimiliki nchi nzuri ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaapia baba zako,
sw.B: Fanya yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anayaona kuwa sawa na mema, ili mambo yakuendee vema, nawe uweze kuingia na kuimiliki nchi nzuri ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaapia baba zako,
sw.R: Fanya yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anasema ni sawa na mema. Ndipo mambo yatakuendea vizuri. Utaingia na kuichukua iwe yako nchi nzuri aliyowaahidi mababu zako kwa kiapo.

decisions.choice: in the eyes of the LORD: as the LORD judges it
decisions.reason: What is right in God's eyes is what he sees as right, set against what is right in one's own eyes (12:8, 25, 28).

decisions.choice: so that ... you may go in and take possession: the gift of the land and obedience go together
decisions.reason: The result clauses tie Israel's well-being and its entry into the land to doing what is right (4:1; 8:1; 11:8).

decisions.choice: what the LORD sees as right (Balanced); what the LORD says is right; he promised (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "in the eyes of" plainly and uses "he" for the second mention of the LORD.

source.text: לַהֲדֹ֥ף אֶת־כָּל־אֹיְבֶ֖יךָ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: to thrust out all your enemies from before you, just as spoke Yahweh.

en.L: to thrust out all your enemies from before you, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.
en.B: driving out all your enemies before you, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised.
en.R: Your enemies will be driven out ahead of you, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised.

es.L: para echar a todos tus enemigos de delante de ti, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho.
es.B: expulsando a todos tus enemigos delante de ti, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo prometió.
es.R: Tus enemigos serán expulsados delante de ti, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo prometió.

fr.L: pour chasser tous tes ennemis devant toi, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a dit.
fr.B: en chassant tous tes ennemis devant toi, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a promis.
fr.R: Tes ennemis seront chassés devant toi, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a promis.

sw.L: kuwafukuza adui zako wote mbele yako, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema.
sw.B: kwa kuwafukuza adui zako wote mbele yako, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoahidi.
sw.R: Adui zako watafukuzwa mbele yako, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoahidi.

decisions.choice: to thrust out: the driving out of the enemies that comes with taking the land
alternatives: the LORD will thrust out your enemies
you will thrust out your enemies
decisions.reason: The infinitive does not say who drives the enemies out. God promised to drive them out before Israel (Exodus 23:27-31; 34:11), and Israel was to take part (7:1-2); both may be in view.

decisions.choice: thrust out: push away, drive off
decisions.reason: The verb means to push or shove (Numbers 35:20). Here it pictures the enemy peoples pushed out ahead of Israel.

decisions.choice: spoken: promised
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: Your enemies will be driven out
decisions.reason: Readable uses a passive, which, like the Hebrew, leaves open who drives them out.

source.text: כִּֽי־יִשְׁאָלְךָ֥ בִנְךָ֛ מָחָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר מָ֣ה הָעֵדֹ֗ת וְהַֽחֻקִּים֙ וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: When asks you your son tomorrow, saying, what [are] the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments which commanded Yahweh our God you?

en.L: When your son asks you in time to come, saying, 'What [are] the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has commanded you?'
en.B: Some day your son will ask you, 'What do they mean, these decrees, statutes and rulings that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has commanded you?'
en.R: Someday your son will ask you, 'Why did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God give you these instructions, laws, and rules?'

es.L: Cuando te pregunte tu hijo mañana, diciendo: “¿Qué [son] los testimonios y los estatutos y los juicios que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} ha mandado?”
es.B: Algún día tu hijo te preguntará: “¿Qué significan estos decretos, estatutos y normas que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} ha ordenado?”
es.R: Algún día tu hijo te preguntará: “¿Por qué {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} dio estas instrucciones, leyes y normas?”

fr.L: Quand ton fils te demandera demain, en disant : “Que [sont] les témoignages, et les prescriptions, et les jugements que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu vous a commandés ?”
fr.B: Un jour, ton fils te demandera : “Que signifient ces décrets, ces prescriptions et ces règles que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu vous a commandés ?”
fr.R: Un jour, ton fils te demandera : “Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu vous a-t-il donné ces instructions, ces lois et ces règles ?”

sw.L: Mwanao atakapokuuliza kesho, akisema, 'Ni nini shuhuda, na kanuni, na hukumu ambazo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu amewaamuru ninyi?'
sw.B: Siku moja mwanao atakuuliza, 'Masharti haya, kanuni na maagizo ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu amewaamuru yana maana gani?'
sw.R: Siku moja mwanao atakuuliza, 'Kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu aliwapa maelekezo haya, sheria na maagizo?'

decisions.choice: tomorrow: in time to come
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 13:14, "tomorrow" here means some time in the future.

decisions.choice: the child's question: the teaching of the next generation
decisions.reason: The same pattern of question and answer is found in Exodus 12:26-27, 13:14 and Joshua 4:6-7, 21-23. The question gives the parent the opening to tell the story that verses 21-25 give.

decisions.choice: What are ...: what do they mean, why were they given
decisions.reason: The son does not ask what the laws say but what lies behind them. The answer is not a list of rules but the story of the exodus.

decisions.choice: commanded you: the reading of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The son speaks to his parents as those to whom the law was first given. The ancient Greek translation reads "commanded us", which may smooth the change of person. The Hebrew reading is kept; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: What do they mean (Balanced); Why did ... give you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the son's question as a question about meaning and purpose, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לְבִנְךָ֔ עֲבָדִ֛ים הָיִ֥ינוּ לְפַרְעֹ֖ה בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וַיּוֹצִיאֵ֧נוּ יְהוָ֛ה מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם בְּיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will say to your son, slaves we were to Pharaoh in Egypt, and brought us out Yahweh from Egypt by a hand strong.

en.L: then you shall say to your son, 'Slaves we were to Pharaoh in Egypt, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought us out from Egypt with a strong hand.
en.B: Then tell your son, 'In Egypt we were slaves to Pharaoh, but by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strong hand {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} led us out of Egypt.
en.R: Then tell your son, 'We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to bring us out of Egypt.

es.L: entonces dirás a tu hijo: “Esclavos éramos del faraón en Egipto, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos sacó de Egipto con mano fuerte.
es.B: Entonces dile a tu hijo: “En Egipto éramos esclavos del faraón, pero con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano poderosa {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos sacó de Egipto.
es.R: Entonces dile a tu hijo: “Éramos esclavos del faraón en Egipto. Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} usó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gran poder para sacarnos de Egipto.

fr.L: alors tu diras à ton fils : “Esclaves, nous l’étions de Pharaon en Égypte, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a fait sortir d’Égypte par une main forte.
fr.B: Alors dis à ton fils : “En Égypte, nous étions esclaves de Pharaon, mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a fait sortir d’Égypte par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main puissante.
fr.R: Alors dis à ton fils : “Nous étions esclaves de Pharaon en Égypte. Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est servi de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grande puissance pour nous faire sortir d’Égypte.

sw.L: ndipo utamwambia mwanao, 'Watumwa tulikuwa kwa Farao huko Misri, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akatutoa Misri kwa mkono wenye nguvu.
sw.B: Ndipo umwambie mwanao, 'Huko Misri tulikuwa watumwa wa Farao, lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alitutoa Misri kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wenye nguvu.
sw.R: Ndipo umwambie mwanao, 'Tulikuwa watumwa wa Farao huko Misri. Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alitumia nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kuu kututoa Misri.

decisions.choice: Slaves we were: the answer starts with the story
decisions.reason: "Slaves" is placed first. The parent answers the question about the laws by telling what God did; the laws rest on the rescue (5:6, 15).

decisions.choice: we ... us: the later generation speaks as those rescued
decisions.reason: The parent speaks in the first person, though the child's generation was born after the exodus. Each generation counts itself among those God brought out (5:3).

decisions.choice: a strong hand: great power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power in action, here God's power against Pharaoh (4:34; 5:15; 7:8).

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level, for Israel's slavery in Egypt, as in verse 12.

decisions.choice: by his strong hand (Balanced); used his great power (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced names whose hand it is; Readable says what "a strong hand" means, as Exodus 13:14 does.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן יְהוָ֡ה אוֹתֹ֣ת וּ֠מֹפְתִים גְּדֹלִ֨ים וְרָעִ֧ים׀בְּמִצְרַ֛יִם בְּפַרְעֹ֥ה וּבְכָל־בֵּית֖וֹ לְעֵינֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Yahweh signs and wonders great and harmful against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against all his household, before our eyes.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave signs and wonders, great and harmful, against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against all his household, before our eyes.
en.B: We saw it with our own eyes: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought great and devastating signs and wonders on Egypt, on Pharaoh and on all his household.
en.R: We saw {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do great and terrible miracles. They brought disaster on Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on everyone in his palace.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo señales y prodigios, grandes y dañinos, contra Egipto, contra el faraón y contra toda su casa, ante nuestros ojos.
es.B: Lo vimos con nuestros propios ojos: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} envió señales y prodigios grandes y devastadores sobre Egipto, sobre el faraón y sobre toda su casa.
es.R: Vimos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} hacer milagros grandes y terribles. Trajeron desastre sobre Egipto, sobre el faraón y sobre todos los de su palacio.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait des signes et des prodiges, grands et funestes, contre l’Égypte, contre Pharaon et contre toute sa maison, sous nos yeux.
fr.B: Nous l’avons vu de nos propres yeux : {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a frappé l’Égypte, Pharaon et toute sa maison de signes et de prodiges grands et dévastateurs.
fr.R: Nous avons vu {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} faire de grands et terribles miracles. Ils ont fait venir le malheur sur l’Égypte, sur Pharaon et sur tous les gens de son palais.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akafanya ishara na maajabu, makubwa na mabaya, juu ya Misri, juu ya Farao, na juu ya nyumba yake yote, mbele ya macho yetu.
sw.B: Tuliona kwa macho yetu wenyewe: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alileta ishara na maajabu makubwa na yenye maangamizi juu ya Misri, juu ya Farao na juu ya nyumba yake yote.
sw.R: Tulimwona {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akifanya miujiza mikubwa na ya kutisha. Miujiza hiyo ilileta msiba juu ya Misri, juu ya Farao na juu ya kila mtu katika ikulu yake.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the plagues on Egypt
decisions.reason: The pair names the acts of power God did in Egypt, which showed who he is (4:34; 7:19; Exodus 7:3).

decisions.choice: harmful: bringing disaster
decisions.reason: The word usually means "bad" or "evil". Here it describes signs that brought harm and ruin on Egypt, not anything wrong in God's acts.

decisions.choice: his household: Pharaoh's family and court
decisions.reason: A king's house included his family and his officials (Exodus 7:28-29; 12:30).

decisions.choice: before our eyes: we saw it
decisions.reason: Israel had seen these things for itself (4:34; 11:7).

decisions.choice: devastating (Balanced); terrible (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "devastating" and "terrible" for the Hebrew "bad", which here means bringing disaster; Readable adds what they brought.

decisions.choice: everyone in his palace
decisions.reason: Readable says who "his household" were.

source.text: וְאוֹתָ֖נוּ הוֹצִ֣יא מִשָּׁ֑ם לְמַ֨עַן֙ הָבִ֣יא אֹתָ֔נוּ לָ֤תֶת לָ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖ע לַאֲבֹתֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And us he brought out from there so as to bring us, to give to us the land which he swore to our fathers.

en.L: And us {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought out from there in order to bring us in, to give us the land which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to our fathers.
en.B: Us, though, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led out from there, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could bring us in and give us the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to our fathers.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought us out of Egypt so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could bring us into the land and give it to us, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised our ancestors.

es.L: Y a nosotros nos sacó de allí para traernos, para darnos la tierra que juró a nuestros padres.
es.B: A nosotros, en cambio, nos sacó de allí para traernos aquí y darnos la tierra que había jurado a nuestros padres.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos sacó de Egipto para traernos a esta tierra y dárnosla, como lo había prometido a nuestros antepasados.

fr.L: Et nous, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a fait sortir de là pour nous faire entrer, pour nous donner le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a juré à nos pères.
fr.B: Mais nous, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a fait sortir de là, afin de nous faire entrer et de nous donner le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait juré à nos pères.
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a fait sortir d’Égypte pour nous faire entrer dans ce pays et nous le donner, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’avait promis à nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}.

sw.L: Na sisi alitutoa huko ili atuingize, atupe nchi aliyowaapia baba zetu.
sw.B: Lakini sisi alitutoa huko ili atuingize na kutupa nchi aliyowaapia baba zetu.
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alitutoa Misri ili atuingize katika nchi hii na kutupa, kama alivyokuwa amewaahidi mababu zetu.

decisions.choice: us: set against Egypt and Pharaoh
decisions.reason: "Us" is placed first, in contrast with the Egyptians struck by the signs in verse 22.

decisions.choice: brought out in order to bring in
decisions.reason: The rescue from Egypt had a goal: God freed Israel to give it the promised land (Exodus 3:8; 6:6-8).

decisions.choice: But the LORD ... out of Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD, since after verse 22 a plain "he" could be taken for Pharaoh, and names the place "there" refers to.

source.text: וַיְצַוֵּ֣נוּ יְהוָ֗ה לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַחֻקִּ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה לְיִרְאָ֖ה אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לְט֥וֹב לָ֨נוּ֙ כָּל־הַיָּמִ֔ים לְחַיֹּתֵ֖נוּ כְּהַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded us Yahweh to do all the statutes these, to fear Yahweh our God, for good to us all the days, to preserve us alive as [at] the day this.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, for our good all the days, to keep us alive, as [at] this day.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded us to keep all these statutes and to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, for our good always, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might keep us alive, as we are today.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded us to obey all these laws and to have deep respect for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. This is for our good, so that we will always do well and stay alive, as we are today.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos mandó poner por obra todos estos estatutos, temer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, para nuestro bien todos los días, para conservarnos la vida, como [en] este día.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos mandó guardar todos estos estatutos y temer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, para nuestro bien siempre, a fin de conservarnos con vida, como lo estamos hoy.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos mandó obedecer todas estas leyes y tener un profundo respeto por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios. Esto es para nuestro bien, para que siempre nos vaya bien y sigamos con vida, como estamos hoy.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a commandé de pratiquer toutes ces prescriptions, de craindre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, pour notre bien tous les jours, pour nous garder en vie, comme [en] ce jour.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a commandé de garder toutes ces prescriptions et de craindre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, pour notre bien à toujours, afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous garde en vie, comme nous le sommes aujourd’hui.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a commandé d’obéir à toutes ces lois et d’avoir un profond respect pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu. C’est pour notre bien, pour que tout aille toujours bien pour nous et que nous restions en vie, comme nous le sommes aujourd’hui.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alituamuru kuzitenda kanuni hizi zote, kumcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, kwa mema yetu siku zote, ili kutuhifadhi hai, kama [ilivyo] siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alituamuru tuzishike kanuni hizi zote na kumcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, kwa faida yetu daima, ili atuhifadhi hai, kama tulivyo leo.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alituamuru tutii sheria hizi zote na kumheshimu sana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu. Hili ni kwa faida yetu, ili mambo yatuendee vizuri siku zote na tuendelee kuishi, kama tulivyo leo.

decisions.choice: for our good: the laws serve Israel's well-being
decisions.reason: The statutes are given for Israel's benefit, not as a burden (10:13; 30:15-16).

decisions.choice: to keep us alive: God preserves the life of those who keep his laws
decisions.reason: The infinitive continues the purpose: God commanded these things so that Israel might live (4:1; 8:1; Leviticus 18:5).

decisions.choice: as at this day: as is now the case
decisions.reason: The phrase points to the present: Israel is alive and cared for, as it is today (2:30; 4:20).

decisions.choice: fear
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: have deep respect for
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: so that he might keep us alive (Balanced); stay alive (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced names God as the one who keeps Israel alive, as the Hebrew form implies; Readable says what this means for Israel.

source.text: וּצְדָקָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶה־לָּ֑נוּ כִּֽי־נִשְׁמֹ֨ר לַעֲשׂ֜וֹת אֶת־כָּל־הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֗את לִפְנֵ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּֽנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And righteousness it will be for us if we take care to do all the commandment this before Yahweh our God, just as he commanded us.

en.L: And righteousness it will be for us, if we take care to do all this commandment before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has commanded us.'
en.B: Righteousness will be ours if we take care to keep this whole commandment in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded us.'
en.R: We will be righteous before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God if we take care to obey all these commands, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told us.'

es.L: Y justicia será para nosotros, si cuidamos de poner por obra todo este mandamiento delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, tal como nos ha mandado.”
es.B: Esa será nuestra justicia, si cuidamos de cumplir todo este mandamiento en presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, como nos lo ordenó.”
es.R: Seremos justos delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios si cuidamos de obedecer todos estos mandamientos, tal como nos lo dijo.”

decisions.choice: righteousness: being in the right before God
alternatives: it will be counted to our credit
we will be in the right
decisions.reason: Righteousness here is the standing of those who live as God's covenant requires, recognized by him. Keeping the law does not earn the rescue, which came first (verses 21-23); it is Israel's faithful answer to it. Deuteronomy 24:13 uses the same words of a kindness that "will be righteousness for you before the LORD"; compare Genesis 15:6.

decisions.choice: this commandment: the whole of the law, in the singular
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: before the LORD: in his presence and in his sight
decisions.reason: Israel's obedience is lived out before God, who sees it (verse 18; 24:13).

decisions.choice: We will be righteous before the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says "righteous" for "righteousness will be ours", the same sense in a simpler sentence; it turns the singular "commandment" into "commands", as in verse 1.

decisions.choice: closing single quote
decisions.reason: The parent's answer to the son, opened in verse 21, closes here. Moses' own speech, begun at 5:1, continues past this chapter, so no double quote closes.
